_comment: The single record of how every chartsymbols.xml symbol token chartcore's
derive/ used to bake maps onto the vendored quantenschaum icon set --- the
migration to ONE icon source (see PORT-MAP.md for the prose).
`port`  : a vendored icon in ./ ; derive emits this name directly.
`gap`   : no vendored equivalent, so the symbol was TRACED from
chartsymbols.xml's own HPGL. These lived in ./placeholder/ and
were day-colour-baked until task xytoltso recoloured all 16 onto
role hexes and moved them into ./ --- they are now real,
themeable catalogue entries like `drawn`, and both ./placeholder/
and `placeholders.json`'s worklist are empty. What still sets
them apart is their PIVOT-INFLATED canvas, which must never be
composited (icons::pack::TRACED_LITERAL_KEYS).
`drawn` : no vendored equivalent existed and none was appropriate, so the
artwork was DRAWN for mivnav (task lppokvtq) and lives in ./ under
the S-52 token's own name. Real, themeable vector art through the
normal role-sentinel path --- NOT placeholders, and not in
placeholders.json.
`drop`  : intentionally no symbol (area fill / pattern / not a point icon).
HARD RULE for `port`: the icon MUST NOT be a parametric ATON shape asset
(a `COLORING{}` template --- barrel, cylinder, tower, can,
conical, spar, sphere, ...). Those are buoy/beacon/topmark
bodies, addressed ONLY through derive::aton's composed numeric
form `BOYSHP/6/0/3`; named bare they draw the uncoloured
template, which is how PRDARE ended up rendering a barrel BUOY
(wyzqklzz). The `-lmk` files exist for the land-structure
meanings of those words. Pinned by tests/
derive_symbol_coverage.rs::
no_derive_symbol_names_a_bare_parametric_icon.
`origin` records where the token's artwork came from in chartsymbols.xml:
V = HPGL vector definition (traced directly)
R = raster-only bitmap     (the trace follows the bitmap, not the HPGL)
- = not a <symbol> at all  (area/line pattern name, handled separately)

DGPS01DRFSTA01.why: run-together name, defined as a <symbol> nowhere. chartsymbols.xml's own Paper row for the same feature (RCID 30507) spells out the intent: SY(RDOSTA02);TX('DGPS'), i.e. the ordinary radio mast plus a DGPS label. stations.rs emits that.

FLTHAZ02.why: floating hazard; not a <symbol> in chartsymbols.xml or any SymbolPatch, so there is no artwork to trace and never was. s57-style.json's OBSTRN layer answers the same question for the same rows --- CATOBS 6,7 -> foul, everything else -> obstruction.

TNKCON02.note: was `cylinder` --- a PARAMETRIC topmark template (TOPSHP_5), which drew an uncoloured topmark, not a tank. s57-style.json's own `silo-point` layer answers `building` for every CATSIL but 4 (wyzqklzz).

TNKFRM01.note: was `barrel` --- a PARAMETRIC buoy-shape template (BOYSHP_6), so a tank farm drew a barrel BUOY; this is the bug the user reported (wyzqklzz). No vendored tank-farm pictogram exists and upstream gives PRDARE no point icon at all, so this follows TNKCON rather than drawing nothing. Still `low`: a real tank-farm glyph would be better, but it must not be a parametric shape word.

TOWERS01.note: was bare `tower` --- a PARAMETRIC beacon-shape template (BCNSHP_3). `tower-lmk` is CATLMK_17, the landmark tower artwork lndmrk.rs already uses for the same structure (wyzqklzz).

RESTRN51.note: was a `gap`: the atlas crop is a magenta anchor with a slash, i.e. the symbol no-anchor.svg already draws --- and RESTRN01's identical arm was mapped onto it all along (lppokvtq).

LIGHTS81.why: strip light (CATLIT 9). Known gap, predates this migration.

QUESMRK1.why: directional light question-mark. Known gap, predates this migration.

ISODGR51.why: isolated-danger promotion (aidsHazards.ts). Settings-dependent symbology, the one place chart symbology tracks user config --- so it was the highest-priority raster to kill.

DANGER51.why: depth-based wreck/obstruction danger pick, shallower than safety contour. wreck-dangerous.svg's own ellipse, mast marks removed.

DANGER52.why: the same ellipse unfilled --- deeper than the safety contour.

DANGER53.why: the same ellipse over an intertidal fill --- OBSTRN04's WATLEV 4/5 (covers and uncovers) arm. Not a <symbol> anywhere; the fill follows chartsymbols.xml's own OBSTRN01 (ADEPVSBCHBLK) vs OBSTRN03 (ADEPITBCHBLK) distinction.

LOWACC03.why: CSQUAPNT01's catch-all low-accuracy '?' plus leader. Not a <symbol>; redrawn to the QUAPOS02/03 conventions off LOWACC01, which upstream's SLCONS03 uses for the identical QUAPOS range.

LNDARE01.why: land area fill, not a point symbol.

ESSARE01.why: LC() line complex, defined only in chartsymbols.xml's <line-styles>. restricted.rs writes it as `lc` and deliberately emits no centred symbol for CATREA 27/28 (divergence D8), so the point symbol the SY(ESSARE01) instruction asks for was never missing --- it does not exist upstream either.

NAVARE51.why: LC() line complex, same as ESSARE01: 43 uses in chartsymbols.xml and every one of them an LC(), plus one <line-styles> definition. Never a point symbol.

CBLSUB06.why: LC() line pattern -> vendored `cable` line-pattern tile (cablesPipelines.ts), not a point icon.

PIPARE51.why: AP() area pattern; pattern migration is a separate, later stage.

PIPARE61.why: AP() area pattern; pattern migration is a separate, later stage.

WRECKS07.why: the 'depth unknown' overbar is not drawn at all. Rendered centre-anchored it floated detached ABOVE the wreck (bar at the top of a 32x24 canvas, wreck symbols 16x6/16x16), so keeping it needed a second offset fix on top of a redraw. User decision, task lppokvtq: a QUASOU=7 wreck selects the vendored wreck-dangerous symbol instead --- which is also what s57-style.json layer 122's CATWRK DEFAULT arm does.
